- initial `index-*.js`: 192.7 KiB gzip;
- `WorkshopPage-*.js`: 48.0 KiB gzip;
- `DemoPage-*.js`: 2.6 KiB gzip;
- CSS: 11.2 KiB gzip.

The workshop keeps its existing Phase 3 structure: four-stage navigation, plan outline, working document, activity/evidence rail. The visual layer changed; the stage and approval semantics did not.

## 3. Static serving and assets

`src/server/index.ts` serves `dist/web` when it exists:

- `/` → `index.html`.
- real files → their content type.
- unknown non-API paths → `index.html` (SPA fallback).
- `/api/*` is never served from disk.
- Path resolution is checked against the `dist/web` root to prevent traversal.
- Private state under `UB_DATA_DIR` is outside the static root and is never served.

Public hero assets are produced by `scripts/build-hero-assets.py`:

```text
assets/source/hero-ghostlight-workshop.webp   (master, not shipped)
        │
        ├─ public/assets/hero/hero-ghostlight-wide-{1920,1280,768}.{avif,webp}
        ├─ public/assets/hero/hero-ghostlight-wide-{1280,768}.jpg
        └─ public/assets/hero/hero-ghostlight-portrait-{900,600}.{avif,webp}
```

Vite copies `public/` to `dist/web/`, so production URLs are `/assets/hero/...`. The `<picture>` element selects the portrait crop below 720px and wide crops above it. Explicit width/height and CSS aspect ratios prevent layout shift.

## 4. Frontend modules

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `src/web/App.tsx` | Route switch, lazy loading, page title |
| `src/web/routes.ts` | Pure path resolution and titles |
| `src/web/landing/` | Hero, usage modes, spirit roster, deterministic teaser, setup, privacy, FAQ, final CTA |
| `src/web/demo/` | Scripted walkthrough, all-state gallery, recovery states |
| `src/web/workshop/` | Real Oracle/Architect/Maker/Witness workflow |
| `src/web/components/SpiritCharacter.tsx` | Original inline SVG characters and state classes |
| `src/web/components/RunInspector.tsx` | Native runs, evidence ledger, permission boundary |
| `src/web/components/SpiritStageTabs.tsx` | Semantic four-stage navigation |
| `src/web/components/SectionCard.tsx` | Outline cards and empty state |
| `src/web/components/SetupCommandTabs.tsx` | Accessible command tabs |
| `src/web/components/SetupDialog.tsx` | Native `<dialog>` setup help |
| `src/web/components/Brand.tsx` | Brand mark and type lockup |
| `src/web/spirits.ts` | Spirit profiles and state labels |
| `src/web/content/landing.ts` | Landing copy, fixtures, recommendations, FAQ |
| `src/web/setup.ts` | Tested setup command data |
| `src/web/styles.css` | Tokens, components, character states, responsive and accessibility rules |

The landing and demo import only browser-safe modules. `WorkshopProject` is a type-only import from `src/web/api.ts`; no server module enters the client bundle.

## 5. State and evidence flow

The API contract is unchanged from Phase 3:

- Every mutation sends `actionId` and `expectedRevision`.
- Browser mutations require `x-ub-session-token`, issued by `/api/session` over loopback (or after basic auth in a hosted deployment).
- Approvals target an exact section version and hash.
- A revision supersedes the old approval and invalidates dependent sections.
- Maker requires all current sections approved plus a separate scope grant.
- Runs are recorded as operations; unknown runs are reconciled, not repeated.
- Evidence records an observed native result; a missing result is an empty state.

The Run Inspector is read-only. The only write it can trigger is the existing reconcile action for an unknown operation. It cannot approve, retry, or grant permission.

## 6. Workflow authorization is unchanged

Phase 4 did not change:

- session-token checks;
- basic-auth behavior;
- revision conflicts;
- exact-version approval checks;
- Maker scope gating;
- native permission authority;
- atomic project storage.

The setup dialog and landing page are instructions only. Opening them does not assert that OpenCode is reachable.

## 7. Why the demo is separate

The deterministic demo renders fixture data with visible “scripted sample” labels. It exists because a first-time visitor should understand the interface before installing an engine, and because visual regression tests need stable states that do not depend on a model call. It is a separate route so the real workshop cannot accidentally use fixture data.

## 8. Not in this architecture

- A second coding harness or command executor.
- A public arbitrary-execution sandbox.
- Remote access to a visitor's local repository.
- A database service.
- Automatic publication or submission.
- A heavy animation or 3D framework.

# Decision ledger

**Scope:** Phase 4 interface, landing, visual system, motion, and spirit characters.
**Last updated:** 2026-10-31.

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D4-01 | Use the **Ghostlight Hacker Workshop** theme | Generic SaaS landing, bright productivity app, pure terminal | Fits the existing haunted-workshop product while keeping a readable contemporary interface | Deep navy foundation, amber work light, spectral blue accents, layered paper/blueprint/glass/terminal surfaces |
| D4-02 | Keep the landing page at `/` and the real workshop at `/workshop` | Replace the workshop with a landing page; use a hash route | A first-time visitor needs a product explanation; the workshop needs a stable direct URL | Three routes (`/`, `/demo`, `/workshop`) with SPA fallback |
| D4-03 | Add a separate deterministic demo at `/demo` | Put fixture controls inside the real workshop; use a video only | Keeps fixture data out of the live workflow and gives visual tests stable states | The demo is explicitly labeled; it never calls a model |
| D4-04 | Lazy-load the workshop and demo | One large bundle | Landing is the first visit; workshop-specific Motion/API code should not block it | Initial JS 192.7 KiB gzip; workshop chunk 48.0 KiB; demo 2.6 KiB |
| D4-05 | Do not add an animation framework | GSAP, Lottie, Rive, Three.js | Motion and CSS already cover entry, state, and transitions; measured need is low | No new runtime; animation stays small and state-bound |
| D4-06 | Draw the four spirits as original inline SVG | Generated character images; copied mascots | Crisp at every size, tiny, themeable, accessible, state-driven, and provably original | Characters are code in `SpiritCharacter.tsx`; every state is a class |
| D4-07 | Generate one original hero image with the authorized image tool | Pure CSS landscape; stock photo; no hero image | The prompt calls for a cinematic workshop with atmospheric depth and copy space; generation was authorized | Master + responsive AVIF/WebP/JPEG outputs, prompt/provenance documented; no text/logos/watermarks |
| D4-08 | Keep source masters out of the shipped bundle | Ship the master and resize in the browser | Avoids multi-hundred-KiB downloads and layout shift | `assets/source/` is separate from `public/assets/hero/`; explicit dimensions in `<picture>` |
| D4-09 | Use semantic stage navigation, not disabled buttons | Keep disabled tab buttons | Disabled buttons are skipped by keyboard focus and imply interactivity | `<nav><ol><li aria-current="step">` with mini spirits and state text |
| D4-10 | Use native `<dialog>` for setup help | Custom modal | Built-in focus trapping, Escape behavior, and backdrop semantics | Opening help never implies the engine is connected |
| D4-11 | Use tabbed setup commands with roving tabindex | Static code blocks | The landing must show several tested commands without a wall of code | Arrow/Home/End keyboard support and copy action |
| D4-12 | Keep workflow authorization untouched | Refactor auth while restyling | Phase 3 semantics are working and security-sensitive | No changes to session-token checks, exact-version approvals, Maker scope, or native permission authority |
| D4-13 | Make the deterministic demo read-only | Let visitors run fake actions | Fake actions would undermine the honesty claim | Fixture controls step through states; real actions live in `/workshop` |
| D4-14 | Commit Playwright visual snapshots | Manual screenshots only | The prompt requires visual snapshots and keyboard/contrast/reduced-motion checks | `npm run test:visual`; snapshots in `tests/visual/snapshots/` |
| D4-15 | Prefer system Chrome/Chromium for visual tests, with Playwright fallback | Require a fixed browser download | Works in the verified Linux environment without a second browser install | `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE` is honored; otherwise Playwright's browser is used |
| D4-16 | Do not use fabricated social proof | Testimonials, counts, awards | The product has no measured users or endorsements | Landing copy states the absence of fabricated claims |
| D4-17 | Remove Node `--watch` from the default dev script | Keep watch and require `.env` | Pinned Node crashes watching a missing `.env`; default setup must work from a clean checkout | `npm run dev` is stable; `npm run dev:watch` is opt-in with `.env` |
| D4-18 | Keep the hero image decorative and put all meaning in HTML | Put product copy in the image | Accessibility, localization, and performance | Hero `<picture>` is `aria-hidden`; headings and CTAs are real text |

## Open follow-ups (not Phase 5 work)

- A real recorded demo and final submission assets remain separate acceptance work.
- The free-model route remains account-dependent and time-limited.
- A public hosted URL is not asserted until a deployment is verified.
- Any future change to the asset budget or claims requires updating `docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` and `docs/PRODUCT_BRIEF.md`.

# Unfinished Business

**Turn unfinished ideas into hackathon-ready builds.**

Unfinished Business is an OpenCode-powered hackathon project builder. Four friendly spirits guide one idea through a clear proposal, an approved plan, a real bounded build, and evidence you can defend.

![Ghostlight Hacker Workshop landing page](tests/visual/snapshots/landing-wide.png)

## What it is

- A **landing page** at `/` that explains the product, the four roles, OpenCode's role, and the two honest usage paths.
- A **deterministic walkthrough** at `/demo` with scripted fixture data, every spirit state, and representative recovery/error states. It does not call a model.
- The **real workshop** at `/workshop`, which connects to a local OpenCode server and records what actually happened.

OpenCode supplies the agent loop, model access, native tools, permissions, execution, interruption, and native sessions. Unfinished Business adds the four-stage workshop, exact-version approvals, dependency invalidation, evidence views, and the Ghostlight interface. It does **not** ship a second coding harness or a general command executor.

| Spirit | Role |
|---|---|
| Oracle | Clarify an idea into a product proposal and open questions |
| Architect | Draft one planning section and wait for approval of that exact version |
| Maker | Perform an approved, bounded native edit through OpenCode |
| Witness | Inspect evidence in a fresh session and prepare honest review drafts |

## Two ways to use it

**Hosted demo or private deployment** — a labeled deterministic sample, or a private, password-protected workshop using the server's own isolated demo workspace. It does not reach into a visitor's local repository, and it is not a public execution sandbox.

**Full local mode** — the browser app, local API, and pinned OpenCode server on your machine over loopback. Maker's edit in this release is bounded to an isolated demo workspace. App approval never overrides an OpenCode permission denial.

The intended model route is OpenCode's free DeepSeek model, `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`. It is time-limited and must be verified on your own account. No paid fallback is configured.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: Linux, Node **22.14+**, npm, a supported OpenCode 2.x server, and a free-model route on your account.

```bash
npm ci
cp .env.example .env
```

Terminal 1 — OpenCode:

```bash
./node_modules/@opencode/cli-linux-x64-baseline/bin/opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
```

Terminal 2 — API:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Terminal 3 — interface:

```bash
npm run dev:web
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`.

For a single production process:

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:4200/`. The detailed, tested guide is [docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md](docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md).

## Verification

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run budget
npm run test:visual
```

Current Phase 4 results (2026-10-31):

- 30 unit/integration/component tests pass.
- 12 Playwright visual/accessibility tests pass with 21 committed snapshots.
- Initial JS is **192.7 KiB gzip**; CSS **11.2 KiB gzip**; all hero variants **570.9 KiB** total.
- Keyboard focus order, dialog Escape, setup tab arrow keys, 200% text zoom, 390px overflow, reduced motion, and token contrast are checked.

`npm run test:visual` needs a Chromium executable. It prefers `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE`, then system Chrome/Chromium, then Playwright's browser.

## Status

The guided workflow, native execution path, recovery, and evidence ledger are implemented. Phase 4 adds the Ghostlight landing page, visual system, characters, motion, deterministic demo, and visual/accessibility tests. A live free-model run was not repeated during the Phase 4 interface work; the previous native execution evidence remains the workflow record.

A real recorded demo, final article/video, and submission packaging remain separate acceptance work. A public hosted URL is not asserted here. Hosted and private deployment configuration is in [docs/HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md).

## Documentation

- [Product brief](docs/PRODUCT_BRIEF.md) — positioning, landing claims, two usage paths.
- [UX and visual system](docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md) — theme, tokens, components, character states, motion, accessibility, asset prompt/provenance, performance budget.
- [Local setup](docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md) — tested commands and troubleshooting.
- [Hosted deployment](docs/HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md) — Render/private instance, secrets, security boundary.
- [Demo and submission](docs/DEMO_AND_SUBMISSION.md) — approved screenshots, capture guidance, claim rules.
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — routes, asset loading, evidence flow, unchanged authorization.
- [Decisions](docs/DECISIONS.md) — Phase 4 design decisions and alternatives.
- [Implementation plan](docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) — phase history, work units, verification gate.
- [Changelog](docs/CHANGELOG.md) — Phase 4 changes.
- [Engineering blueprint](docs/ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md) — canonical implementation plan and amendments.
- [Product idea packet](docs/Unfinished-Business-Idea-Packet-v1.md) — approved product scope and decisions.
- [Sentry and OpenCode setup](docs/SENTRY_AND_OPENCODE_SETUP.md) — release/source-map and password matching.
- [Render deployment](docs/RENDER_DEPLOYMENT.md) — original deployment notes.
- [Complete local prompt set](docs/prompts/README.md) — Prompts 0–3 and project overrides.

## Development policy

- Repository: [kernelKain/unfinished-business](https://github.com/kernelKain/unfinished-business).
- Work on the existing `main` branch. Do not create phase branches.
- Complete and verify each phase, then make one commit for that phase before starting the next phase.
- Steps are work/checklist units, not individual commits. Commit subjects describe the change without phase or step numbering.
- Preserve unrelated changes. A blocked commit blocks entry to the next implementation phase; do not bypass access restrictions.
- No fabricated testimonials, usage figures, awards, or live-run claims.
- No second coding harness, remote repository mount, or public arbitrary-execution sandbox.

## Delivery

The first release targets a local browser on Linux. A real recorded demonstration and a reproducible local-start guide provide judge access; hosted code execution is outside this release. Backboard, Sentry Agent Tracing, and Entire remain selected partner targets, with qualification conditional on meaningful actual use and evidence.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Dependency, prompt, and asset attribution must be checked before redistribution. The generated hero asset's prompt and provenance are documented in [docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md](docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md).

`findSelectedModel`.

```
const [connection, setConnection] = useState<ConnectionStatus|null>(null);

...
```

But our UI can show onboarding instead of workshop when `setupOpen` or firstRun. However user might want to browse workshop despite no engine. The incoming behavior auto-opens onboarding on first run, which is good but our landing "Open workshop" then shows onboarding, not the stage UI. Our Playwright visual test expects workshop h1 "What's still haunting" with engine unreachable. If onboarding auto-opens when no discovery, test breaks. Their onClose button says "Continue to workshop" for firstRun but does nothing to bypass. Hmm. We can add `const [onboardingDismissed, setOnboardingDismissed] = useState(false)` and condition `(setupOpen || (firstRun && !onboardingDismissed && state !== unavailable))`; onClose sets both false/dismissed. This lets user continue with warning. Good.

connected = connection?.state === "connected" || "degraded"

dot live if connected; warning if degraded; else false
```

# OpenCode integration contract

Status: Phase 2 integration contract. This document describes the tested surface, not every endpoint OpenCode exposes.

## Supported versions and client

| Component | Tested value | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode server | `2.0.32` | Major `2` is accepted. A different `2.x` version is shown as `degraded` with an explicit untested-version warning. Major `1.x`, unparseable versions, and other majors are `incompatible_version` and discovery stops. |
| `@opencode/client` | `2.0.32` | Exact lockfile version. The client is generated from the same HTTP contract as the server. |
| Node.js | `>=22.14` | The app runtime. |

The opt-in live diagnostic records the actual server version and API surface:

```bash
OPENCODE_LIVE_DIAGNOSTIC=1 \
OPENCODE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4096 \
OPENCODE_PASSWORD='the server password' \
npm run diagnose:opencode
```

It performs no prompt or model inference. It creates, reads, and removes one disposable empty session when a model is available. Without `OPENCODE_LIVE_DIAGNOSTIC=1` it prints `SKIP` and exits 0.

### Live diagnostic result recorded for this phase

Against a disposable OpenCode `2.0.32` server with `@opencode/client 2.0.32`:

- `/api/info` returned server `2.0.32`.
- The catalog returned 2 providers, 9 models, 4 visible agents, 2 commands, and 31 skills.
- `session.create`, `session.get`, and `session.remove` succeeded for a disposable empty session. No prompt was sent.
- `session.fork` on an empty session is rejected by the server (`empty_session`). Fork is therefore offered only for sessions with at least one message.
- `session.compact` queues a compaction and can later report `compaction.unavailable` when there is nothing to compact.
- `session.interrupt` returns `{ interrupted: false }` for an idle session.
- `session.revert.stage` requires a real message boundary; an unknown message returns `MessageNotFoundError`.
- No provider API key was read, logged, or returned.

This is a compatibility proof for those calls. It is not proof that every provider/model can complete inference.

## Endpoints used

All calls are made by the application server, never directly by the browser. The application sends HTTP Basic authentication only when a server password is configured. OpenCode's fixed Basic-auth username is `opencode`.

| Purpose | Endpoint(s) |
|---|---|
| Version and identity | `GET /api/info` |
| Model catalog | `GET /api/model` |
| Provider catalog | `GET /api/provider` |
| Provider connection state | `GET /api/integration` |
| Agents | `GET /api/agent` |
| Pending permissions | `GET /api/permission/request`, `POST /api/session/:sessionID/permission/:requestID/reply` |
| Commands | `GET /api/command` |
| Skills | `GET /api/skill` |
| MCP servers | `GET /api/mcp` |
| Formatter/LSP configuration | `GET /api/config` |
| Session create | `POST /api/session` |
| Session read/resume | `GET /api/session/:sessionID` |
| Session messages | `GET /api/session/:sessionID/message` |
| Session interrupt | `POST /api/session/:sessionID/interrupt` |
| Session fork | `POST /api/session/:sessionID/fork` |
| Session compact | `POST /api/session/:sessionID/compact` |
| Session revert | `POST /api/session/:sessionID/revert/stage`, `DELETE /api/session/:sessionID/revert`, `POST /api/session/:sessionID/revert/commit` |
| Prompt/wait/generate | `POST /api/session/:sessionID/prompt`, `POST /api/experimental/session/:sessionID/wait`, `POST /api/session/:sessionID/generate` |
| Diff | `GET /api/session/:sessionID/diff` |

Session actions are restricted to native sessions referenced by the active project (`project.nativeSessions` and operation records). The API does not enumerate or control arbitrary OpenCode sessions.

## Connection states

`not_configured` → no URL has been checked. `checking` is reserved for an in-flight check. `connected` means the server answered, the major version is compatible, the catalog was read, and no warning remains. `degraded` means the server answered but there is an untested patch version, a provider that needs authentication, a pending permission, a selected-model problem, or a partial capability probe. `authentication_required` means OpenCode rejected the connection with 401. `incompatible_version` means the major version is not supported. `unavailable` means the server did not answer or returned a transport/origin/invalid-response failure.

Every non-connected state includes at least one diagnostic with an actionable repair. The UI never replaces a failed check with an optimistic connected state.

## Provider and model discovery

The server catalog is normalized into a product-safe shape. These values are dropped before leaving the server:

- provider `settings`, `headers`, and `body` (they can contain `apiKey` or base URLs);
- model `settings`, `headers`, `body`, and request compatibility internals not needed by the UI;
- skill contents (only id/name/description are retained);
- raw config entries (only formatter/LSP names and disabled flags are retained);
- session context, prompt text, and message bodies outside the project's own operation flow.

Normalized facts:

| Fact | Rule |
|---|---|
| Key | `providerID/modelID`; a variant is appended as `#variant` only for display. |
| Display name | OpenCode `name`. |
| Availability | `enabled !== false` and the provider is not disabled. |
| Pricing | `free` only when every reported cost row has zero input/output/cache prices; `paid` when any price is non-zero; `unknown` when no cost rows are reported. |
| Local | Known local provider IDs (`ollama`, `lmstudio`, `vllm`, `llamacpp`, `local`) or a loopback provider `baseURL`. Otherwise `null`, not a fabricated `false`. |
| Limits | Context, input, and output from `limit`, or `null`. |
| Modalities | `capabilities.input` and `capabilities.output`. |
| Tools | `capabilities.tools`. |
| Reasoning | `supported: true` when `compatibility.reasoningField`/`requireReasoning` is present, or when the model reports variants. Otherwise `null` (unknown). The source is shown. |
| Variants | Exact reported variant IDs only. There is no universal low/medium/high scale. |
| Provider readiness | `needs_auth` only when an OpenCode integration connection says so; otherwise inferred from the catalog and shown as inferred/unknown. |

Provider API keys and quota remain OpenCode's responsibility. The application does not call credential endpoints and does not accept provider keys in any request body.

## Credentials ownership

| Secret | Owner | Where it may live |
|---|---|---|
| Provider API keys / OAuth tokens | OpenCode | OpenCode credential store / XDG data directory. Never in Unfinished Business. |
| OpenCode server Basic-auth password | The person running OpenCode | `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` for non-interactive deployments, or in-memory only when entered in the wizard. No browser storage, project JSON, logs, Sentry events, or exports. |
| Application access password | Deployment | `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD` in the deployment secret store. |
| Browser mutation token | Application | `UB_SESSION_TOKEN`, returned only to an authenticated/loopback browser session and used in a request header. Not persisted by the browser UI. |

The wizard has no provider-key field. A request that includes `providerKey`, `apiKey`, or a similar unknown field is rejected with a message explaining that provider keys belong in OpenCode.

## Application roles

OpenCode remains the execution engine. Unfinished Business maps its four product roles to explicit OpenCode agents:

| Application role | Preferred custom agent | Tested fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oracle | `oracle` / `ub-oracle` | `plan` | Clarify and propose a product scope without editing. |
| Architect | `architect` / `ub-architect` | `plan` | Draft one section at a time with read-only tools. |
| Maker | `maker` / `ub-maker` | `build` | Perform the approved, bounded edit in the isolated demo workspace. |
| Witness | `witness` / `ub-witness` | `plan` | Review evidence from a fresh session. |

The mapping is discovered from `/api/agent`; the current mapping and fallback are shown in the OpenCode panel. If neither a custom agent nor the fallback is visible, session creation uses OpenCode's default and the limitation is visible.

Read-only roles receive session permissions denying `edit`, `shell`, and `external_directory`. Maker receives `edit` allowed while `shell` and `external_directory` remain denied. These application rules supplement, but do not replace, OpenCode's own permission engine.

## Permissions

Pending requests are read from OpenCode and filtered to project-owned sessions. The UI offers `Allow once`, `Always`, and `Reject`; it never auto-approves. `Always` asks OpenCode to save the proposed pattern, which may be broad. The application cannot override a configured `deny`.

## Sessions, usage, and deferred controls

- **List/resume** is restricted to project-owned sessions.
- **Interrupt** is exposed for the selected project session and for an active Maker run. The run manager marks cancellation and keeps the operation `CANCELLED` even if completion arrives afterward.
- **Fork** is available only for a session with messages. A new fork is returned to the advanced panel but is not silently rebound to a product role.
- **Compact** queues a compaction. OpenCode may report `compaction.unavailable` for a short session.
- **Revert** requires a message ID. Stage/clear/commit are advanced controls with explicit confirmation-shaped actions; OpenCode enforces busy/empty-session errors.
- **Usage** is shown only when OpenCode returns session cost/token values. Quota and balance are not exposed by the HTTP API; the panel links to the provider console.
- **Tool catalog** is deferred because OpenCode `2.0.32` does not expose a separate HTTP tool list. Tool exposure is governed by the selected agent and permissions.
- **Formatter/LSP status** is configuration presence only; it is not a live health check.
- **Session list of arbitrary sessions** is deliberately not exposed.

## Version-dependent gaps

These gaps are recorded rather than papered over:

- Other `2.x` patch versions are accepted but marked degraded until the live diagnostic is rerun.
- `@opencode/client` 2.0.32's generated types are the compatibility baseline. A newer server may shape optional fields differently.
- `session.fork` rejects an empty session; the UI disables the action when the message count is zero.
- OpenCode may report `variant: "default"` on a session even when no variant was requested. The UI treats this as the model default, not a fabricated variant.
- Cost/token totals depend on provider usage reporting. A zero value is shown only when OpenCode actually reports it.
- The shared public demo must not ask visitors for provider keys; a public deployment without a connected provider will legitimately show no models.

# Unfinished Business

**Bring your ideas to life.**

A local browser companion built on OpenCode's open-source coding harness. Four friendly spirits guide a builder from an unfinished idea through an approved plan, real implementation, verification, and submission drafts.

| Spirit | Role |
|---|---|
| Oracle | Clarify an idea and approve a useful product scope |
| Architect | Present one planning section, revise it, and wait for approval before continuing |
| Maker | Use OpenCode to perform approved work and show actual results |
| Witness | Review evidence and prepare honest final materials |

OpenCode provides the agent loop, model access, tools, permissions, and native sessions. Unfinished Business adds the workshop interface, stage progression, versioned approvals, decision history, evidence views, and a safe first-run connection/discovery experience.

## Status

Phase 2 is implemented: a clean user can connect a compatible OpenCode server, repair authentication, inspect providers/models/capabilities, choose a supported model and reported reasoning variant, and start a bounded Maker run. The Phase 1 asynchronous run lifecycle is the prerequisite: runs return immediately, persist their state, survive a restart as `UNKNOWN`, and are never silently replayed.

The application no longer assumes a fixed model. Models, providers, limits, modalities, tools, variants, and availability are discovered from OpenCode. The chosen model is stored per project and recorded in Maker operation and evidence records. A v1 project with the old fixed-model hint migrates safely; the hint is used only if OpenCode still reports that model.

Provider API keys stay in OpenCode. The application accepts only the OpenCode server Basic-auth password, holds it in memory (or reads `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` for non-interactive starts), and never writes it to project JSON, browser storage, logs, events, Sentry, or exports.

## Requirements

- Node.js `>=22.14`
- OpenCode `2.x`; tested with `2.0.32`
- Linux for the first release (the lockfile includes the Linux baseline CLI)

## Quick start

```bash
npm ci
```

Start OpenCode in one terminal:

```bash
opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
```

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` if you want non-interactive settings. Then:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. The first-run wizard asks for the server URL and the password printed by `opencode serve`. Provider accounts are connected inside OpenCode with `/connect`, then a model is chosen with `/models`. The wizard lists only the catalog OpenCode reports.

For the built app:

```bash
npm run build && npm start
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4200`. Set `UB_PORT` if `4200` is taken. Project data stays in `UB_DATA_DIR` (default `.unfinished-business/`), which is gitignored.

## Documentation

- [OpenCode integration contract](docs/OPENCODE_INTEGRATION.md) — exact tested version/API surface, credentials ownership, discovery, roles, permissions, sessions, limitations.
- [Local setup](docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md) — install/start/connect/provider/model steps and troubleshooting.
- [Hosted deployment](docs/HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md) — private-hosted credential handling and public-demo restrictions.
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — configuration and trust boundaries.
- [UX and visual system](docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md) — onboarding and advanced-control states.
- [Decisions](docs/DECISIONS.md), [implementation plan](docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md), and [changelog](docs/CHANGELOG.md).
- [Engineering blueprint](docs/ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md) — historical phase record and evidence.
- [Product idea packet](docs/Unfinished-Business-Idea-Packet-v1.md) — approved product scope.
- [Complete local prompt set](docs/prompts/README.md) — Prompts 0–3 and project context.
- [Project Prompt 1](docs/prompts/PROMPT_1_ARCHITECT.md) — project-specific Architect instructions.

## Verification

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
```

The test suite covers the asynchronous run lifecycle, connection state and URL/version policy, provider/model normalization, secret redaction, fixed-model migration, model/variant validation, onboarding HTTP flow, session authorization, and the existing workflow/recovery/contracts/prompt checks.

An opt-in live compatibility check is available:

```bash
OPENCODE_LIVE_DIAGNOSTIC=1 \
OPENCODE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4096 \
OPENCODE_PASSWORD='the server password' \
npm run diagnose:opencode
```

It performs no prompt or model inference; it may create/read/remove one disposable empty session. Without the opt-in flag it prints `SKIP`.

## Hosted deployments

`UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` selects the policy:

- `local` — first-run connection editing, loopback HTTP allowed.
- `hosted-private` — connection managed by environment/secret store; read-only browser configuration; OpenCode credentials in its persistent XDG data.
- `hosted-demo` — read-only connection and no provider-key prompts; may legitimately show no models.

The existing password-protected Render service is a private hosted deployment. See [docs/HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md).

## Development policy

- Repository: [kernelKain/unfinished-business](https://github.com/kernelKain/unfinished-business).
- Work on the existing `main` branch. Do not create phase branches.
- Complete and verify each phase, then make one commit for that phase before starting the next phase.
- Commit subjects describe the change without phase or step numbering.
- Preserve unrelated changes. A blocked commit blocks entry to the next implementation phase; do not bypass access restrictions.

Phase 2 stops at its handoff. Phase 3 independent acceptance, publication, and submission work has not started.

## Delivery

The first release targets a local browser on Linux. A real recorded demonstration and a reproducible local-start guide provide judge access; hosted code execution is outside this release. Backboard, Sentry Agent Tracing, and Entire remain selected partner targets, with qualification conditional on meaningful actual use and evidence.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Dependency, prompt, and asset attribution must be checked before redistribution.

| Commands | `GET /api/command` |
| Skills | `GET /api/skill` |
| MCP servers | `GET /api/mcp` |
| Formatter/LSP configuration | `GET /api/config` |
| Session create | `POST /api/session` |
| Session read/resume | `GET /api/session/:sessionID` |
| Session messages | `GET /api/session/:sessionID/message` |
| Session interrupt | `POST /api/session/:sessionID/interrupt` |
| Session fork | `POST /api/session/:sessionID/fork` |
| Session compact | `POST /api/session/:sessionID/compact` |
| Session revert | `POST /api/session/:sessionID/revert/stage`, `DELETE /api/session/:sessionID/revert`, `POST /api/session/:sessionID/revert/commit` |
| Prompt/wait/generate | `POST /api/session/:sessionID/prompt`, `POST /api/experimental/session/:sessionID/wait`, `POST /api/session/:sessionID/generate` |
| Diff | `GET /api/session/:sessionID/diff` |

Session actions are restricted to native sessions referenced by the active project (`project.nativeSessions` and operation records). The API does not enumerate or control arbitrary OpenCode sessions.

## Connection states

`not_configured` → no URL has been checked. `checking` is reserved for an in-flight check. `connected` means the server answered, the major version is compatible, the catalog was read, and no warning remains. `degraded` means the server answered but there is an untested patch version, a provider that needs authentication, a pending permission, a selected-model problem, or a partial capability probe. `authentication_required` means OpenCode rejected the connection with 401. `incompatible_version` means the major version is not supported. `unavailable` means the server did not answer or returned a transport/origin/invalid-response failure.

Every non-connected state includes at least one diagnostic with an actionable repair. The UI never replaces a failed check with an optimistic connected state.

## Provider and model discovery

The server catalog is normalized into a product-safe shape. These values are dropped before leaving the server:

- provider `settings`, `headers`, and `body` (they can contain `apiKey` or base URLs);
- model `settings`, `headers`, `body`, and request compatibility internals not needed by the UI;
- skill contents (only id/name/description are retained);
- raw config entries (only formatter/LSP names and disabled flags are retained);
- session context, prompt text, and message bodies outside the project's own operation flow.

Normalized facts:

| Fact | Rule |
|---|---|
| Key | `providerID/modelID`; a variant is appended as `#variant` only for display. |
| Display name | OpenCode `name`. |
| Availability | `enabled !== false` and the provider is not disabled. |
| Pricing | `free` only when every reported cost row has zero input/output/cache prices; `paid` when any price is non-zero; `unknown` when no cost rows are reported. |
| Local | Known local provider IDs (`ollama`, `lmstudio`, `vllm`, `llamacpp`, `local`) or a loopback provider `baseURL`. Otherwise `null`, not a fabricated `false`. |
| Limits | Context, input, and output from `limit`, or `null`. |
| Modalities | `capabilities.input` and `capabilities.output`. |
| Tools | `capabilities.tools`. |
| Reasoning | `supported: true` when `compatibility.reasoningField`/`requireReasoning` is present, or when the model reports variants. Otherwise `null` (unknown). The source is shown. |
| Variants | Exact reported variant IDs only. There is no universal low/medium/high scale. |
| Provider readiness | `needs_auth` only when an OpenCode integration connection says so; otherwise inferred from the catalog and shown as inferred/unknown. |

Provider API keys and quota remain OpenCode's responsibility. The application does not call credential endpoints and does not accept provider keys in any request body.

## Credentials ownership

| Secret | Owner | Where it may live |
|---|---|---|
| Provider API keys / OAuth tokens | OpenCode | OpenCode credential store / XDG data directory. Never in Unfinished Business. |
| OpenCode server Basic-auth password | The person running OpenCode | `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` for non-interactive deployments, or in-memory only when entered in the wizard. No browser storage, project JSON, logs, Sentry events, or exports. |
| Application access password | Deployment | `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD` in the deployment secret store. |
| Browser mutation token | Application | `UB_SESSION_TOKEN`, returned only to an authenticated/loopback browser session and used in a request header. Not persisted by the browser UI. |

The wizard has no provider-key field. A request that includes `providerKey`, `apiKey`, or a similar unknown field is rejected with a message explaining that provider keys belong in OpenCode.

## Application roles

OpenCode remains the execution engine. Unfinished Business maps its four product roles to explicit OpenCode agents:

| Application role | Preferred custom agent | Tested fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oracle | `oracle` / `ub-oracle` | `plan` | Clarify and propose a product scope without editing. |
| Architect | `architect` / `ub-architect` | `plan` | Draft one section at a time with read-only tools. |
| Maker | `maker` / `ub-maker` | `build` | Perform the approved, bounded edit in the isolated demo workspace. |
| Witness | `witness` / `ub-witness` | `plan` | Review evidence from a fresh session. |

The mapping is discovered from `/api/agent`; the current mapping and fallback are shown in the OpenCode panel. If neither a custom agent nor the fallback is visible, session creation uses OpenCode's default and the limitation is visible.

Read-only roles receive session permissions denying `edit`, `shell`, and `external_directory`. Maker receives `edit` allowed while `shell` and `external_directory` remain denied. These application rules supplement, but do not replace, OpenCode's own permission engine.

## Permissions

Pending requests are read from OpenCode and filtered to project-owned sessions. The UI offers `Allow once`, `Always`, and `Reject`; it never auto-approves. `Always` asks OpenCode to save the proposed pattern, which may be broad. The application cannot override a configured `deny`.

## Sessions, usage, and deferred controls

- **List/resume** is restricted to project-owned sessions.
- **Interrupt** is exposed for the selected project session and for an active Maker run. The run manager marks cancellation and keeps the operation `CANCELLED` even if completion arrives afterward.
- **Fork** is available only for a session with messages. A new fork is returned to the advanced panel but is not silently rebound to a product role.
- **Compact** queues a compaction. OpenCode may report `compaction.unavailable` for a short session.
- **Revert** requires a message ID. Stage/clear/commit are advanced controls with explicit confirmation-shaped actions; OpenCode enforces busy/empty-session errors.
- **Usage** is shown only when OpenCode returns session cost/token values. Quota and balance are not exposed by the HTTP API; the panel links to the provider console.
- **Tool catalog** is deferred because OpenCode `2.0.32` does not expose a separate HTTP tool list. Tool exposure is governed by the selected agent and permissions.
- **Formatter/LSP status** is configuration presence only; it is not a live health check.
- **Session list of arbitrary sessions** is deliberately not exposed.

## Version-dependent gaps

These gaps are recorded rather than papered over:

- Other `2.x` patch versions are accepted but marked degraded until the live diagnostic is rerun.
- `@opencode/client` 2.0.32's generated types are the compatibility baseline. A newer server may shape optional fields differently.
- `session.fork` rejects an empty session; the UI disables the action when the message count is zero.
- OpenCode may report `variant: "default"` on a session even when no variant was requested. The UI treats this as the model default, not a fabricated variant.
- Cost/token totals depend on provider usage reporting. A zero value is shown only when OpenCode actually reports it.
- The shared public demo must not ask visitors for provider keys; a public deployment without a connected provider will legitimately show no models.

# Unfinished Business

**Bring your ideas to life.**

A local browser companion built on OpenCode's open-source coding harness. Four friendly spirits guide a builder from an unfinished idea through an approved plan, real implementation, verification, and submission drafts.

| Spirit | Role |
|---|---|
| Oracle | Clarify an idea and approve a useful product scope |
| Architect | Present one planning section, revise it, and wait for approval before continuing |
| Maker | Use OpenCode to perform approved work and show actual results |
| Witness | Review evidence and prepare honest final materials |

OpenCode provides the agent loop, model access, tools, permissions, and native sessions. Unfinished Business adds the workshop interface, stage progression, versioned approvals, decision history, evidence views, and a safe first-run connection/discovery experience.

## Status

Phase 2 is implemented: a clean user can connect a compatible OpenCode server, repair authentication, inspect providers/models/capabilities, choose a supported model and reported reasoning variant, and start a bounded Maker run. The Phase 1 asynchronous run lifecycle is the prerequisite: runs return immediately, persist their state, survive a restart as `UNKNOWN`, and are never silently replayed.

The application no longer assumes a fixed model. Models, providers, limits, modalities, tools, variants, and availability are discovered from OpenCode. The chosen model is stored per project and recorded in Maker operation and evidence records. A v1 project with the old fixed-model hint migrates safely; the hint is used only if OpenCode still reports that model.

Provider API keys stay in OpenCode. The application accepts only the OpenCode server Basic-auth password, holds it in memory (or reads `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` for non-interactive starts), and never writes it to project JSON, browser storage, logs, events, Sentry, or exports.

## Requirements

- Node.js `>=22.14`
- OpenCode `2.x`; tested with `2.0.32`
- Linux for the first release (the lockfile includes the Linux baseline CLI)

## Quick start

```bash
npm ci
```

Start OpenCode in one terminal:

```bash
opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
```

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` if you want non-interactive settings. Then:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. The first-run wizard asks for the server URL and the password printed by `opencode serve`. Provider accounts are connected inside OpenCode with `/connect`, then a model is chosen with `/models`. The wizard lists only the catalog OpenCode reports.

For the built app:

```bash
npm run build && npm start
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4200`. Set `UB_PORT` if `4200` is taken. Project data stays in `UB_DATA_DIR` (default `.unfinished-business/`), which is gitignored.

## Documentation

- [OpenCode integration contract](docs/OPENCODE_INTEGRATION.md) — exact tested version/API surface, credentials ownership, discovery, roles, permissions, sessions, limitations.
- [Local setup](docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md) — install/start/connect/provider/model steps and troubleshooting.
- [Hosted deployment](docs/HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md) — private-hosted credential handling and public-demo restrictions.
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — configuration and trust boundaries.
- [UX and visual system](docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md) — onboarding and advanced-control states.
- [Decisions](docs/DECISIONS.md), [implementation plan](docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md), and [changelog](docs/CHANGELOG.md).
- [Engineering blueprint](docs/ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md) — historical phase record and evidence.
- [Product idea packet](docs/Unfinished-Business-Idea-Packet-v1.md) — approved product scope.
- [Complete local prompt set](docs/prompts/README.md) — Prompts 0–3 and project context.
- [Project Prompt 1](docs/prompts/PROMPT_1_ARCHITECT.md) — project-specific Architect instructions.

## Verification

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
```

The test suite covers the asynchronous run lifecycle, connection state and URL/version policy, provider/model normalization, secret redaction, fixed-model migration, model/variant validation, onboarding HTTP flow, session authorization, and the existing workflow/recovery/contracts/prompt checks.

An opt-in live compatibility check is available:

```bash
OPENCODE_LIVE_DIAGNOSTIC=1 \
OPENCODE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4096 \
OPENCODE_PASSWORD='the server password' \
npm run diagnose:opencode
```

It performs no prompt or model inference; it may create/read/remove one disposable empty session. Without the opt-in flag it prints `SKIP`.

## Hosted deployments

`UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` selects the policy:

- `local` — first-run connection editing, loopback HTTP allowed.
- `hosted-private` — connection managed by environment/secret store; read-only browser configuration; OpenCode credentials in its persistent XDG data.
- `hosted-demo` — read-only connection and no provider-key prompts; may legitimately show no models.

The existing password-protected Render service is a private hosted deployment. See [docs/HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md).

## Development policy

- Repository: [kernelKain/unfinished-business](https://github.com/kernelKain/unfinished-business).
- Work on the existing `main` branch. Do not create phase branches.
- Complete and verify each phase, then make one commit for that phase before starting the next phase.
- Commit subjects describe the change without phase or step numbering.
- Preserve unrelated changes. A blocked commit blocks entry to the next implementation phase; do not bypass access restrictions.

Phase 2 stops at its handoff. Phase 3 independent acceptance, publication, and submission work has not started.

## Delivery

The first release targets a local browser on Linux. A real recorded demonstration and a reproducible local-start guide provide judge access; hosted code execution is outside this release. Backboard, Sentry Agent Tracing, and Entire remain selected partner targets, with qualification conditional on meaningful actual use and evidence.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Dependency, prompt, and asset attribution must be checked before redistribution.

1: # Unfinished Business
2: 
3: **Turn unfinished ideas into hackathon-ready builds.**
4: 
5: Unfinished Business is an OpenCode-powered hackathon project builder. Four friendly spirits guide one idea through a clear proposal, an approved plan, a real bounded build, and evidence you can defend.
6: 
7: ![Ghostlight Hacker Workshop landing page](tests/visual/snapshots/landing-wide.png)
8: 
9: ## What it is
10: 
11: - A **landing page** at `/` that explains the product, the four roles, OpenCode's role, and the two honest usage paths.
12: - A **deterministic walkthrough** at `/demo` with scripted fixture data, every spirit state, and representative recovery/error states. It does not call a model.
13: - The **real workshop** at `/workshop`, which connects to a local OpenCode server and records what actually happened.
14: 
15: OpenCode supplies the agent loop, model access, native tools, permissions, execution, interruption, and native sessions. Unfinished Business adds the four-stage workshop, exact-version approvals, dependency invalidation, evidence views, and the Ghostlight interface. It does **not** ship a second coding harness or a general command executor.
16: 
17: | Spirit | Role |
18: |---|---|
19: | Oracle | Clarify an idea into a product proposal and open questions |
20: | Architect | Draft one planning section and wait for approval of that exact version |
21: | Maker | Perform an approved, bounded native edit through OpenCode |
22: | Witness | Inspect evidence in a fresh session and prepare honest review drafts |
23: 
24: ## Two ways to use it
25: 
26: **Hosted demo or private deployment** — a labeled deterministic sample, or a private, password-protected workshop using the server's own isolated demo workspace. It does not reach into a visitor's local repository, and it is not a public execution sandbox.
27: 
28: **Full local mode** — the browser app, local API, and pinned OpenCode server on your machine over loopback. Maker's edit in this release is bounded to an isolated demo workspace. App approval never overrides an OpenCode permission denial.
29: 
30: The intended model route is OpenCode's free DeepSeek model, `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`. It is time-limited and must be verified on your own account. No paid fallback is configured.
31: 
32: ## Quick start
33: 
34: Prerequisites: Linux, Node **22.14+**, npm, a supported OpenCode 2.x server, and a free-model route on your account.
35: 
36: ```bash
37: npm ci
38: cp .env.example .env
39: ```
40: 
41: Terminal 1 — OpenCode:
42: 
43: ```bash
44: ./node_modules/@opencode/cli-linux-x64-baseline/bin/opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
45: ```
46: 
47: Terminal 2 — API:
48: 
49: ```bash
50: npm run dev
51: ```
52: 
53: Terminal 3 — interface:
54: 
55: ```bash
56: npm run dev:web
57: ```
58: 
59: Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`.
60: 
61: For a single production process:
62: 
63: ```bash
64: npm run build
65: npm start
66: ```
67: 
68: Then open `http://127.0.0.1:4200/`. The detailed, tested guide is [docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md](docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md).
69:

1: # Architecture — Unfinished Business
2: 
3: **Status:** Implemented through Phase 4. Last updated 2026-10-31.
4: 
5: ## 1. System shape
6: 
7: ```text
8: Browser
9:   ├─ /            landing page (eager)
10:   ├─ /demo        deterministic walkthrough (lazy chunk)
11:   └─ /workshop    real workshop (lazy chunk)
12:         │
13:         │ fetch /api/*  (same origin; mutations carry x-ub-session-token)
14:         ▼
15: Hono server (src/server/app.ts)
16:   ├─ /api/health          public
17:   ├─ /api/project         current snapshot
18:   ├─ /api/engine          OpenCode probe
19:   ├─ /api/messages        stage messages
20:   ├─ /api/approvals       product + Maker scope
21:   ├─ /api/sections/*      revisions + exact-version approvals
22:   ├─ /api/runs/*          Maker run, cancel, reconcile
23:   ├─ /api/export          approved plan + drafts
24:   └─ static dist/web      SPA fallback for non-API paths
25:         │
26:         ▼
27: OpenCode 2.0.32 server over loopback
28:   ├─ model route (free DeepSeek intended)
29:   ├─ native tools and permissions
30:   ├─ sessions/transcripts
31:   └─ isolated demo workspace
32: ```
33: 
34: Unfinished Business never implements a second agent loop, inference client, general command executor, or transcript store. OpenCode owns those. The app owns workflow state, approvals, dependency invalidation, evidence references, and the interface.
35: 
36: ## 2. Frontend routing
37: 
38: `src/web/routes.ts` is the pure route resolver:
39: 
40: | Path | Route | Rendering |
41: |---|---|---|
42: | `/` | `landing` | Eager `LandingPage` |
43: | `/demo` | `demo` | Lazy `DemoPage` |
44: | `/workshop` | `workshop` | Lazy `WorkshopPage` |
45: | anything else | `landing` | Landing fallback |
46: 
47: `src/web/App.tsx` reads `window.location.pathname`, listens for `popstate`, updates `document.title` and `document.documentElement.dataset.route`, and scrolls to the top on route change. Navigations are ordinary anchors, so they work without a client router and the server's SPA fallback can serve `index.html`.
48: 
49: The workshop and demo are split with `React.lazy`. Measured production chunks:
50: 
51: - initial `index-*.js`: 192.7 KiB gzip;
52: - `WorkshopPage-*.js`: 48.0 KiB gzip;
53: - `DemoPage-*.js`: 2.6 KiB gzip;
54: - CSS: 11.2 KiB gzip.
55: 
56: The workshop keeps its existing Phase 3 structure: four-stage navigation, plan outline, working document, activity/evidence rail. The visual layer changed; the stage and approval semantics did not.
57: 
58: ## 3. Static serving and assets
59: 
60: `src/server/index.ts` serves `dist/web` when it exists:
61: 
62: - `/` → `index.html`.
63: - real files → their content type.
64: - unknown non-API paths → `index.html` (SPA fallback).
65: - `/api/*` is never served from disk.
66: - Path resolution is checked against the `dist/web` root to prevent traversal.
67: - Private state under `UB_DATA_DIR` is outside the static root and is never served.
68: 
69: Public hero assets are produced by `scripts/build-hero-assets.py`:
70: 
71: ```text
72: assets/source/hero-ghostlight-workshop.webp   (master, not shipped)
73:         │
74:         ├─ public/assets/hero/hero-ghostlight-wide-{1920,1280,768}.{avif,webp}
75:         ├─ public/assets/hero/hero-ghostlight-wide-{1280,768}.jpg
76:         └─ public/assets/hero/hero-ghostlight-portrait-{900,600}.{avif,webp}
77: ```
78: 
79: Vite copies `public/` to `dist/web/`, so production URLs are `/assets/hero/...`. The `<picture>` element selects the portrait crop below 720px and wide crops above it. Explicit width/height and CSS aspect ratios prevent layout shift.
80: 
81: ## 4. Frontend modules
82: 
83: | Path | Responsibility |
84: |---|---|
85: | `src/web/App.tsx` | Route switch, lazy loading, page title |
86: | `src/web/routes.ts` | Pure path resolution and titles |
87: | `src/web/landing/` | Hero, usage modes, spirit roster, deterministic teaser, setup, privacy, FAQ, final CTA |
88: | `src/web/demo/` | Scripted walkthrough, all-state gallery, recovery states |
89: | `src/web/workshop/` | Real Oracle/Architect/Maker/Witness workflow |
90: | `src/web/components/SpiritCharacter.tsx` | Original inline SVG characters and state classes |
91: | `src/web/components/RunInspector.tsx` | Native runs, evidence ledger, permission boundary |
92: | `src/web/components/SpiritStageTabs.tsx` | Semantic four-stage navigation |
93: | `src/web/components/SectionCard.tsx` | Outline cards and empty state |
94: | `src/web/components/SetupCommandTabs.tsx` | Accessible command tabs |
95: | `src/web/components/SetupDialog.tsx` | Native `<dialog>` setup help |
96: | `src/web/components/Brand.tsx` | Brand mark and type lockup |
97: | `src/web/spirits.ts` | Spirit profiles and state labels |
98: | `src/web/content/landing.ts` | Landing copy, fixtures, recommendations, FAQ |
99: | `src/web/setup.ts` | Tested setup command data |
100: | `src/web/styles.css` | Tokens, components, character states, responsive and accessibility rules |
101: 
102: The landing and demo import only browser-safe modules. `WorkshopProject` is a type-only import from `src/web/api.ts`; no server module enters the client bundle.
103: 
104: ## 5. State and evidence flow
105: 
106: The API contract is unchanged from Phase 3:
107: 
108: - Every mutation sends `actionId` and `expectedRevision`.
109: - Browser mutations require `x-ub-session-token`, issued by `/api/session` over loopback (or after basic auth in a hosted deployment).
110: - Approvals target an exact section version and hash.
111: - A revision supersedes the old approval and invalidates dependent sections.
112: - Maker requires all current sections approved plus a separate scope grant.
113: - Runs are recorded as operations; unknown runs are reconciled, not repeated.
114: - Evidence records an observed native result; a missing result is an empty state.
115: 
116: The Run Inspector is read-only. The only write it can trigger is the existing reconcile action for an unknown operation. It cannot approve, retry, or grant permission.
117: 
118: ## 6. Workflow authorization is unchanged
119: 
120: Phase 4 did not change:
121: 
122: - session-token checks;
123: - basic-auth behavior;
124: - revision conflicts;
125: - exact-version approval checks;
126: - Maker scope gating;
127: - native permission authority;
128: - atomic project storage.
129: 
130: The setup dialog and landing page are instructions only. Opening them does not assert that OpenCode is reachable.
131: 
132: ## 7. Why the demo is separate
133: 
134: The deterministic demo renders fixture data with visible “scripted sample” labels. It exists because a first-time visitor should understand the interface before installing an engine, and because visual regression tests need stable states that do not depend on a model call. It is a separate route so the real workshop cannot accidentally use fixture data.
135: 
136: ## 8. Not in this architecture
137: 
138: - A second coding harness or command executor.
139: - A public arbitrary-execution sandbox.
140: - Remote access to a visitor's local repository.
141: - A database service.
142: - Automatic publication or submission.
143: - A heavy animation or 3D framework.

## 5. Connection, discovery, and deployment modes

`ConnectionService` (`src/server/opencode/connection.ts`) owns the OpenCode server URL, optional in-memory Basic-auth password, version check, and normalized discovery. `src/shared/opencode.ts` validates the browser-safe connection and discovery shapes.

- `local` allows browser connection editing and loopback HTTP.
- `hosted-private` manages the URL/credentials in the environment and makes browser configuration read-only.
- `hosted-demo` is read-only and may legitimately show no models until a provider is connected inside OpenCode.

Discovery normalizes providers, models, agents, roles, permissions, commands, skills, MCP servers, formatter/LSP presence, capabilities, and usage. Provider settings, headers, request bodies, skill contents, and prompt text are dropped before leaving the server. Provider API keys never enter Unfinished Business; only the OpenCode server Basic-auth password may be held in memory. See `docs/OPENCODE_INTEGRATION.md`.

Connection states are `not_configured`, `checking`, `connected`, `authentication_required`, `incompatible_version`, `unavailable`, and `degraded`. Every non-connected state carries at least one diagnostic with a repair action. The UI never replaces a failed check with an optimistic connected state.

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`. Vite proxies `/api` to `http://127.0.0.1:4200` (or `UB_PORT`).

The engine pill in the workshop header reflects `/api/connection`; it shows **OpenCode connected** only after the server answers, the major version is compatible, the catalog is readable, and no warning remains. `degraded`, `authentication_required`, `incompatible_version`, `unavailable`, and `not_configured` each carry a diagnostic and a repair action.

If OpenCode is reachable but no model is selected, `/workshop` opens the first-run connection/model panel. If OpenCode is unavailable, the workshop stays visible with the error and an **Open setup** action; it never invents a connection or a model.

### First-run model selection

1. Start OpenCode and note the server password.
2. Enter the URL (`http://127.0.0.1:4096`) and password in the wizard. The password is held in memory; it is not written to project JSON, browser storage, logs, or Sentry.
3. Provider accounts are connected inside OpenCode with `/connect`; the app never asks for provider API keys.
4. The wizard lists only models that OpenCode reports as available, including free/paid/unknown pricing, context/output limits, modalities, tools, and reported variants.
5. Choose a model and, only if reported, a variant. The selection is stored per project and recorded in Maker operation/evidence records.
6. If the catalog later changes, the app blocks a Maker run until a currently reported model is selected.

## 6. Build and serve one process

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:4200/`. The built app and API share the same server. `npm start` does not start OpenCode; keep the OpenCode server running separately.

## What "local mode" does and does not touch

- Maker's bounded edit targets the isolated demo workspace under `UB_DATA_DIR`, not your repository checkout.
- Project metadata and evidence references live under `UB_DATA_DIR`.
- Native transcripts and sessions stay in OpenCode.
- The browser has no filesystem or shell endpoint.
- App approvals constrain the workflow; they cannot override an OpenCode tool denial.

## Troubleshooting

### `Port 4200 is already in use`

Stop the previous process or set `UB_PORT` to a free port. Vite reads `UB_PORT` when proxying.

### The engine badge says unreachable

1. Confirm OpenCode is listening: `curl http://127.0.0.1:4096/`.
2. Confirm `OPENCODE_BASE_URL` matches.
3. Confirm `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` matches the server.
4. Restart the API after changing `.env`.

### The free model is unavailable

The route is time-limited and account-dependent. The app will not silently switch to a paid model. Check the OpenCode server output and your model access, then retry.

### `npm run dev` exits immediately

This repository's pinned Node needs the non-watch script without `.env`. Use `npm run dev`. If you need watch mode, create `.env` first and use `npm run dev:watch`.

### Vite serves the page but API calls fail

Confirm the API is running on 4200 (or the `UB_PORT` you set) and that Vite was started after the env value was available.

## Verification commands

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run budget
```

The interface's full visual and accessibility check is:

```bash
npm run test:visual
```

It needs a Chromium executable. The config prefers `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE`, then system Chrome/Chromium, then Playwright's installed browser.

46:## Required secrets and values
# Hosted and private deployment

**Status:** Configuration present in `render.yaml`. No public URL is asserted by this document.
**Last updated:** 2026-10-31.

## What a hosted instance is

A hosted instance serves the same build as local mode:

- `/` — the landing page.
- `/demo` — the deterministic walkthrough, clearly labeled as a scripted fixture.
- `/workshop` — the real four-stage workshop.
- `/api/*` — the validated local API.

The instance is **private**: it requires HTTP basic authentication for everything except `/api/health`. The OpenCode server binds to loopback inside the same container. The workshop uses the server's isolated data directory, never a visitor's local repository.

A hosted instance is **not**:

- a public sandbox for arbitrary code execution;
- a remote mount of the visitor's checkout;
- proof that a free model route is available;
- a substitute for the real local workflow when demonstrating actual execution.

## Render configuration

`render.yaml` defines:

| Setting | Value/behavior |
|---|---|
| Runtime | Node 22.14 |
| Build | `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` |
| Start | `npm run start:render` |
| Health check | `/api/health` (public) |
| Disk | 1 GB mounted at `/var/data` |
| Host binding | `UB_HOST=0.0.0.0` |
| Data | `UB_DATA_DIR=/var/data/unfinished-business` |
| Access | `UB_ACCESS_USERNAME` + generated `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD` |
| OpenCode | Generated `OPENCODE_PASSWORD`; loopback `http://127.0.0.1:4096` |
| OpenCode storage | `/var/data/xdg-data`, `/var/data/xdg-config` |
| Sentry | DSN, auth token, and environment supplied as secrets/sync-false values |

`npm run start:render` starts the pinned OpenCode binary on loopback, starts the Hono server, and shuts both down together. If OpenCode exits unexpectedly, the app exits instead of pretending the engine is healthy.

The hosted service is **not compatible with Render's free plan**; it needs a persistent disk and enough memory for the OpenCode runtime.

## Required secrets and values

Set these in the Render dashboard or your deployment secret store. Never commit them.

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD` | Yes in production | The server refuses to start without it when `NODE_ENV=production`. |
| `UB_ACCESS_USERNAME` | Recommended | Defaults to `unfinished-business`. |
| `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` | Yes on Render | `render-start.ts` requires it and passes it to OpenCode. |
| `UB_SESSION_TOKEN` | Recommended | Generated by Render; protects mutations in addition to basic auth. |
| `SENTRY_DSN` | Optional | Server telemetry. |
| `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` | Optional | Browser telemetry. |
| `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` | Required when uploading source maps in a Render build | The Vite config fails the build if `RENDER` is set without it. |
| `SENTRY_RELEASE` | Recommended with auth token | Must match the browser release. |
| `OPENCODE_BASE_URL` | Default `http://127.0.0.1:4096` | Keep loopback. |

content.text: Read around setup panels and perf.

### Empty states

- Dashed border, small glyph, plain title, and an explanation of why empty is correct.
- No illustration that implies content exists.

### Setup panels

- Tabbed commands with roving tabindex, Arrow/Home/End keyboard support, `aria-selected`, and `aria-controls`.
- Commands are sourced from `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md` and the repository scripts.
- Copy button uses the clipboard and provides a visible confirmation.
- Active tab is indicated by border, background, and color, not color alone.

## 4. Character states

Characters are original inline SVG (`src/web/components/SpiritCharacter.tsx`). They are code, not generated images, so they stay crisp, tiny, accessible, and state-driven.

| Spirit | State | Visual | Workflow trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oracle | `idle` | Dim lantern, folded rings | No proposal yet |
| Oracle | `listening` | Rings shimmer, halo breathes | Idea is being read |
| Oracle | `clarification` | Three open question motes | Proposal exists with open questions |
| Architect | `idle` | Compass at rest | Waiting for the next section |
| Architect | `drawing` | Drafting arm moves, blueprint sheet lifts | Section draft or stale review |
| Architect | `approval` | Seal star glows | Exact version approved |
| Maker | `idle` | Tool belt clipped, visor low | No run yet |
| Maker | `building` | Sparks and tapping arm | QUEUED/RUNNING |
| Maker | `permission` | Raised hand + amber keyhole | WAITING_PERMISSION or UNKNOWN |
| Maker | `blocked` | Rose shield with slash | FAILED/CANCELLED/refused |
| Maker | `success` | Mint ring and check | SUCCEEDED |
| Witness | `idle` | Folded wings | No review yet |
| Witness | `scanning` | Lens scan line | Review in progress |

# Implementation plan and phase record

**Last updated:** 2026-10-31.
**Current boundary:** Phase 4 complete and verified. Phase 5 has not started.

## Phase history

| Phase | Outcome | State |
|---|---|---|
| Foundation | Node/Hono/React/Vite shell, atomic project store, shared contracts | Complete |
| Staged workflow | Oracle, Architect, Maker, Witness transitions; exact-version approvals; dependency invalidation | Complete |
| Guided experience | Real native edit path, recovery, Run Inspector data, evidence references | Complete |
| Phase 4 — Ghostlight interface | Landing page, visual system, motion, spirit characters, deterministic demo, visual/accessibility tests | Complete and verified |

## Phase 4 objective

Make the product sell itself as an OpenCode-powered hackathon project builder, explain local and hosted choices honestly, and give the workshop a dimensional, readable, state-driven interface without changing workflow authorization or adding a second coding harness.

## Phase 4 work units

| Unit | Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P4-01 | Verify Phase 3 navigation and preserve stage/approval semantics | Existing workflow tests remain green; stage strip rebuilt as a semantic list |
| P4-02 | Define Ghostlight tokens and component system | `src/web/styles.css`, this docs set |
| P4-03 | Build the landing page and all required sections | `src/web/landing/`, `tests/web.test.ts` |
| P4-04 | Build the deterministic demo and state gallery | `src/web/demo/`, `/demo` route |
| P4-05 | Create hero and character assets | `assets/source/`, `public/assets/hero/`, `SpiritCharacter.tsx`, `scripts/build-hero-assets.py` |
| P4-06 | Apply the system to workshop header, stages, cards, inspector, dialogs, errors, empty states, setup panels | `src/web/workshop/`, shared components |
| P4-07 | Add motion with reduced-motion fallbacks | CSS state classes + Motion seal entry; Playwright reduced-motion test |
| P4-08 | Add component/route and visual/accessibility tests | `tests/web.test.ts`, `tests/visual/landing.spec.ts`, `tests/visual/snapshots/` |
| P4-09 | Measure and document production budget | `scripts/check-budget.mjs`, `docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` |
| P4-10 | Update setup, deployment, product, architecture, decision, demo, README docs | This documentation set |

## Verification gate

Run in this order:

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run budget
npm run test:visual
```

Observed results on 2026-10-31:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Typecheck | PASS |
| Unit/integration/component tests | PASS — 30 tests |
| Production build | PASS |
| Budget | PASS — initial JS 192.7 KiB gzip, all JS 243.2 KiB, CSS 11.2 KiB, hero 570.9 KiB total, largest hero 86.7 KiB |
| Playwright visual/accessibility suite | PASS — 12 tests, 22 snapshots |
| 200% text zoom | PASS |
| 390px overflow | PASS |
| Reduced motion | PASS (`animation: none`) |
| Token contrast (tested pairs) | PASS (≥4.5:1) |
| Setup commands | `npm ci`, `npm run dev`, `npm run dev:web`, build/start verified; OpenCode `--version` and `serve --help` verified |

A live free-model call is not part of the Phase 4 gate. The previous native execution evidence remains the Phase 3 record; Phase 4 did not re-run inference.

## Exit criteria

- A first-time visitor can explain the product, the four roles, OpenCode's role, and the two usage paths.
- The landing page contains tested local setup guidance.
- The interface has visible depth and coherent state-driven motion without harming readability.
- Characters are distinct, original, accessible, and tied to workflow state.
- Reduced-motion and low-bandwidth fallbacks remain complete.
- Production assets meet the documented budget; tests and build pass.
- Workflow authorization is unchanged.

## Next boundary

Stop at Phase 4. Phase 5 is not started and requires a new explicit instruction.

# Changelog

## 2026-10-31 — Ghostlight interface (Phase 4)

### Added

- Landing page at `/` with hero, OpenCode-only positioning, two honest usage paths, four-spirit workflow, deterministic demo teaser, Run Inspector preview, idea-to-tool recommendations, tested local setup tabs, privacy boundary, FAQ, and final CTA.
- Deterministic walkthrough at `/demo` with scripted fixture labels, all-state spirit gallery, fixture evidence, and recovery/error states.
- Original inline SVG Oracle, Architect, Maker, and Witness characters with distinct idle, working, permission, blocked, warning, and success states.
- Ghostlight design tokens for color, type, spacing, radius, elevation, borders, focus, motion, and status.
- Native setup dialog, accessible setup command tabs with copy support, semantic four-stage navigation, section cards, Run Inspector, empty states, and error/warning panels.
- Responsive hero asset pipeline (`scripts/build-hero-assets.py`) with a 21:9 master, AVIF/WebP/JPEG outputs, a 3:4 mobile crop, and explicit dimensions.
- Component/route tests (`tests/web.test.ts`) and Playwright visual/accessibility tests (`tests/visual/landing.spec.ts`) with committed snapshots.
- Production budget check (`scripts/check-budget.mjs`).
- Documentation: product brief, UX/visual system, local setup, hosted deployment, demo/submission guidance, architecture, decisions, implementation plan, changelog.

### Changed

- `App.tsx` is now a small route switch; the workshop moved to `src/web/workshop/WorkshopPage.tsx`.
- Workshop header, stage navigation, outline, document, Activity/evidence rail, and setup affordances use the shared visual system.
- The old single-page workshop stylesheet was replaced by the tokenized Ghostlight system.
- `npm run dev` no longer uses Node watch mode by default; `npm run dev:watch` is opt-in for environments with `.env`.
- README now documents the landing, demo, workshop, and current verification commands.

### Fixed

- Corrected the pinned OpenCode invocation in setup guidance to execute the ELF binary directly.
- Fixed horizontal overflow at 200% text zoom caused by flex-item wrapping in check lists and non-wrapping status chips.
- Fixed mobile header overflow by allowing controlled wrapping.
- Fixed a missing capsule/portrait hero crop for narrow screens.
- Added reduced-motion `animation: none` fallback so character states remain complete without motion.

### Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — pass.
- `npm test` — 30 pass.
- `npm run build` — pass.
- `npm run budget` — pass (initial JS 192.7 KiB gzip; CSS 11.2 KiB; hero 570.9 KiB total).
- `npm run test:visual` — 12 pass, 22 snapshots.
- Keyboard focus order, dialog Escape, setup tab arrow keys, contrast, reduced motion, 200% zoom, and 390px overflow checked by the visual suite.

### Not in this entry

- A live free-model run was not repeated.
- No public hosted URL, testimonial, usage figure, award, or endorsement is claimed.
- Phase 5 was not started.
